clue.text: Do what one is told to control horse in a similar way

indicators.note: to control something is to hold it in, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: to comply is to obey an instruction
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: An instruction to obey orders and rein in a horse just as another rider does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do what one is told' looks like a command to the solver, but it is a phrase for a single verb; the horse is the Arab breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparably is an adverb meaning in a like or equivalent manner.

clue.text: Caught spouse looking round

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
hubby is informal for husband

explanation.surface: Someone catches their husband glancing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking round' seems to mean glancing about, but it means appearing plump.
explanation.definitionFit: Chubby means plump, so a chubby person looks round in shape.

clue.text: Sheep and working dog changing places

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog
on means operating, as a working machine is on
no letters: tells you the two pieces swap from their clue order

explanation.surface: A sheep and a working sheepdog swap positions in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working dog' reads as a sheepdog, but the two words are separate pieces, and the clue tells you to put them the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutton is the meat of a mature sheep, and in old usage the word meant the sheep itself.

clue.text: Blanket covering table

definitions.meaning: first meaning: applying to everything, all-inclusive
second meaning, read literally: stretching over the whole board or table

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a tablecloth; blanket is an adjective meaning comprehensive.
explanation.definitionFit: An across-the-board change is one applying universally, just as a blanket ban covers everything.

clue.text: Vegetable pasta's prepared, but no time to include a bolognese sauce

indicators.note: including something puts it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: the word with its S
ragu is the Italian name for a bolognese meat sauce

explanation.surface: Pasta is made up quickly, with no time to add a bolognese sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: Ragu is the Italian meat sauce that bolognese is a kind of; T is the usual abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is a green vegetable eaten as spears.

clue.text: Sensible cap restricts university courses to begin with

indicators.note: restricting something hems it in, so one piece encloses the other

the remaining letters of lid

explanation.walkthrough: A cap here is a LID, which wraps round UC.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid means clear-headed and rational, which is to say sensible.

clue.text: Article about uncertainty or doubt is lacking in sophistication

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the article is read from right to left

parts.note: the indefinite article
an if is a doubt or condition, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: A newspaper article full of hedging and doubt comes across as unsophisticated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a newspaper piece, but it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: Naif is an adjective meaning naive or artless, without worldly polish.

clue.text: Vegetarian cooked polenta with last of cheese

parts.note: taken as written

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A vegetarian dish of cooked polenta finished with cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vegetarian' looks like a description of the dish, but it is the definition, used as a noun: an antelope eats only plants.
explanation.definitionFit: An antelope is a herbivore, so in a playful sense a vegetarian animal.

clue.text: Agricultural land may spread south of distant road

parts.note: far means distant

parts.note: taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road
no letters: in a down answer, south of means placed below, so the shuffled word follows the distant piece

explanation.surface: Farmland might stretch south of a far-off road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like a verb of possibility, but it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmyard is the enclosed area around farm buildings, a piece of agricultural land.

clue.text: This doctor might make nurse go

definitions.text: This doctor might make nurse go

parts.words: This doctor might make nurse go
parts.note: surface reading: a medic so unpleasant the nurse would quit
setter's reading: these eight letters, treated as malleable and reshaped, form the second word of the answer, so a doctor who reshapes things could turn them into it

explanation.surface: A difficult doctor might drive a nurse to resign.
explanation.walkthrough: Plastic means mouldable; mould NURSE GO and you get SURGEON, so the doctor who works this transformation is the one in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A plastic surgeon reshapes patients' bodies, just as the clue's letters are reshaped.

clue.text: Extreme state

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to say or express in words

explanation.walkthrough: 'Extreme state' reads like a condition of crisis; the two words are separate meanings, an adjective and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter is both an adjective for something total or absolute and a verb meaning to voice or declare.

clue.text: White-collar criminal fleeced investors

parts.note: surface reading: an office fraudster who swindled people who put money in
setter's reading: a professional who embezzles funds entrusted to them, with fleeced pointing at taking money in one's care

explanation.surface: A city fraudster has swindled the people who invested with him.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is close to a plain definition: a peculator embezzles money entrusted to them, the classic white-collar crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A peculator is an embezzler, someone who misappropriates public or entrusted funds.

clue.text: Book series contains line one reads casually

indicators.note: contains says the first pieces hold another piece inside them

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book
a row is a line of things
SER is the abbreviation for series

explanation.surface: A series of books includes a line that someone reads in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: B and SER together hold ROW: B(ROW)SER.
explanation.definitionFit: A browser is a person who looks through books or goods casually rather than with purpose.

clue.text: Express contempt for freedom of movement in demonstration

parts.note: to dis someone is slang for disrespecting them
play is slack, as in a rope with some play in it

explanation.surface: Protesters scorn restrictions on freedom of movement at a demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: A display is a show or exhibition, the same sense as a demonstration of skill.

clue.text: After restructuring, this rep's wage could be what other members of company don't receive

definitions.text: what other members of company don't receive

indicators.note: restructuring rebuilds something in a different order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: After a pay restructuring, one actor's wage is something the rest of the theatre company don't get.
explanation.walkthrough: Company and rep look like business pay talk, but they are a theatre troupe and repertory; a stage whisper is supposedly unheard by the other actors on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: By convention a stage whisper is audible to the audience but not received by the other characters on stage.

clue.text: Exposed snakes exhibited distress

parts.note: snakes as a verb: a path snakes or winds
weeping shows distress

explanation.surface: Someone exposed to snakes was visibly upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Snakes is a verb here, not the reptiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Windswept describes a place exposed to strong winds.

clue.text: Ran newspaper piece about cost of owning property

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: an op-ed is an opinion article; its first three letters
rates are a British local tax charged on property
the last letter of op-ed

explanation.surface: A newspaper article on the cost of owning a home.
explanation.walkthrough: An op-ed is an opinion piece printed opposite the editorial page; British rates were a local tax on property.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate a business is to run it, so operated is a past tense matching ran.

clue.text: Storage medium disrupted by waveform is badly damaged

indicators.note: disrupted means broken into, so another piece is pushed inside

parts.note: a CD is a storage disc; its first letter
a ripple is a small wave
the second letter of CD

explanation.surface: A storage disc disrupted by an electrical wave is badly damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: CD splits round RIPPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Crippled means severely impaired or disabled, so badly damaged.

clue.text: Having taken ecstasy, engineer even represses awkward nature

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rearrange, so the following letters are reworked
taken here means taken away, so one letter is removed from the fodder

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: After taking ecstasy, someone's awkward nature is suppressed, even engineered away.
explanation.walkthrough: One E is removed from EVEN REPRESSES, and the remaining twelve letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Perverseness is a contrary, obstinate disposition, an awkward nature.

clue.text: Utrillo's first seen in National Gallery exhibit

indicators.note: seen in places one piece inside another

parts.note: state, as in national; its first four letters

parts.note: the first letter of the painter's name
the last letter of state

explanation.surface: A painting by Utrillo is first on show at the National Gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: National Gallery reads as the London museum, but it splits: national is STATE, and Gallery starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure, the kind of piece displayed in a gallery.

clue.text: Man briefly rented place in the Alps

indicators.note: briefly says the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a chap is a man
a property let is rented out

explanation.surface: A man spent a short holiday renting somewhere in the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden house of the kind typical of Swiss Alpine villages.

clue.text: Socket on preamp regularly dropped connection

indicators.note: dropping letters at regular intervals keeps only every other one

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of the word
a port is a socket for plugging in a cable

explanation.surface: A socket on an amplifier keeps losing its connection.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer, 'on' puts the socket after the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close, harmonious connection between people.

clue.text: Represent gentleman's exterior to a T

indicators.note: to re-present is to present again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged
exterior means the outside, so only the two end letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of gentleman
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Portray a gentleman's outward appearance exactly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To a T' looks like an idiom for exactly, but T alone is the definition: in the NATO phonetic alphabet T is Tango.
explanation.definitionFit: Tango is the radio code word standing for the letter T in the phonetic alphabet.

clue.text: Revolutionary county court stops time in jail

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the assembled letters are read backwards
to stop something is to plug it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Herts is short for Hertfordshire, an English county
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A revolutionary is jailed by a county court.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is the standard short form of Hertfordshire. 'Time' tempts as a T, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch is slang for a prison sentence, a period served inside.

clue.text: Enact changes to embrace new role and open-mindedness

indicators.note: embracing something means wrapping round it, so one piece goes inside the other
changes says the preceding word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the following word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Changes are enacted to take in a new role and promote open-mindedness.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are rearranged separately, one with 'changes' and one with 'new', before one goes inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is a willingness to accept views differing from one's own, which is open-mindedness.

clue.text: Praise former duty of reporter

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the words, so we go by how they are said

parts.note: a toll is a charge or duty paid, as on a road

explanation.surface: A former journalist praises the duties of a news reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, ex-toll is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, a verb matching praise.

clue.text: Clobber useless individuals

definitions.meaning: first meaning: clothes, from the British slang clobber for gear

explanation.definitionFit: Duds is informal for clothes, and a dud is something or someone that fails to work.

clue.text: Cheat man investing money for group

parts.note: to con is to cheat
tin is old slang for money
a gent is a man
